precepts.text: Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way, and while he opened to us the scriptures? When those scriptures come out, your heart is supposed to be burning for this. How do I get this word out? What ideas do I have? I want to give my time to this truth; everything else outside of this doesn't matter. If your heart is not burning with the word of God, if you don't have desire to want to learn, to want to teach, to better yourself, to better a nation of Israel, you're going to fade away. You're a hireling. You could be 5 years, 10 years, 20 years, but this word is supposed to make your heart burn to get it out.
precepts.point: So this is where you self-examine: am I being a phony, a hypocrite amongst the brethren? Am I walking feignedly? Only you can answer that. You and God know the answer; we don't. If a sister ask us, what about this brother, we can only tell her what you show us. Is he really like that? You got to talk to this guy more in depth, more personally, to find out how they truly are. And some brothers can fake it real good.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
“And they said one to another, Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way, and while he opened to us the scriptures?” When those scriptures come out, your heart is supposed to be burning for this.

How do I get this word out? What ideas do I have? I want to give my time to this truth; everything else outside of this doesn't matter. If your heart is not burning with the word of God, if you don't have the desire to learn, to teach, to better yourself, to better the nation of Israel, you are going to fade away. You're a hireling.

You could be in 5 years, 10 years, 20 years, but this word is supposed to make your heart burn to get it out. The hireling walks feignedly; the one whose heart burns is the one who has known God's fear.

precepts.text: All things must be fulfilled which were written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the Psalms, concerning me; Christ had to fulfil the prophecies written about him.
precepts.point: My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? Why art thou so far from helping me? This is what Christ said when he was on the cross; Christ did not come to do away with the law but to fulfil it.

note.label: Psalm 22: The Prophecy of Christ on the Cross

precepts.why:
“My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?” This is what Christ said on the cross, and he tells why it had to be so: “These are the words which I spake unto you, while I was yet with you, that all things must be fulfilled, which were written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning me.”

All things written in the law of Moses, the prophets, and the psalms concerning him had to be fulfilled. Christ did not come to do away with the law but to fulfil it, and Psalm 22 is one of the psalms written concerning him that he had to fulfil.

precepts.text: All things must be fulfilled, which were written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning me.
precepts.point: What he came to fulfil is the prophecies written concerning him, not the commandments given to Israel to keep. Everything in chapter 2 of this same gospel is an example of that fulfilling.

note.label: Matthew 5: The Sermon on the Mount and the Magnifying of the Law

precepts.why:
Christ said, “Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.” After he rose he told what that fulfilling was: “all things must be fulfilled, which were written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning me.”

What he came to fulfil is what was written concerning him, the prophecies of himself in the law, the prophets and the psalms, not the commandments given to Israel to keep. Everything in chapter 2 of this same gospel, the flight into Egypt, the weeping in Rama, the Nazarene, is an example of that fulfilling. To fulfil is to bring to pass what was foretold, not to do away with the law.

precepts.text: After that he appeared in another form unto two of them, as they walked, and went into the country.
precepts.point: Jesus himself drew near and went with them, but their eyes were holden that they should not know him.

note.label: Luke 24: The Resurrection and the Opening of the Scriptures

precepts.why:
Two of them walked to Emmaus talking of all that had happened, and “Jesus himself drew near, and went with them. But their eyes were holden that they should not know him.”

Mark tells the same walk in a few words: “After that he appeared in another form unto two of them, as they walked, and went into the country.” He appeared in another form. That is why their eyes were holden: the risen Christ walking beside them did not look as they had known him, so two men who had followed him did not know who was with them.

precepts.text: Be not forgetful to entertain strangers: for thereby some have entertained angels unawares.
precepts.point: They walked and talked with him and did not know who he was, which is the plainest picture of what the epistle warns of.

note.label: Luke 24: The Resurrection and the Opening of the Scriptures

precepts.why:
Cleopas answers him as a stranger: “Art thou only a stranger in Jerusalem, and hast not known the things which are come to pass there in these days?” Then he rehearses the whole thing to the very man it happened to: how the chief priests and rulers delivered him to be condemned and crucified, “But we trusted that it had been he which should have redeemed Israel”, the third day, the women at the sepulchre, the vision of angels, the body not found.

They walked and talked with him and did not know who he was. That is the plainest picture of what the epistle warns of: “Let brotherly love continue. Be not forgetful to entertain strangers: for thereby some have entertained angels unawares.” Cleopas and his companion entertained a stranger on the road, and the stranger was Christ himself. Treat the stranger with brotherly love, because you do not know who you are speaking with.

precepts.text: They shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations.
precepts.point: That repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name among all nations, beginning at Jerusalem. It goes among all nations because the people it is for were carried away into all nations.

note.label: Luke 24: The Resurrection and the Opening of the Scriptures

precepts.why:
“all things must be fulfilled, which were written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning me.” He has not yet come back, so those writings are not finished. Then he opened their understanding “that they might understand the scriptures”, and told them “that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name among all nations, beginning at Jerusalem.”

Why among all nations? Because the people it is for were carried away into all nations. He had already told them what would come on Jerusalem: “And they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.” Israel would be led captive into all nations, so the preaching of repentance and remission of sins in his name goes into all nations to find them. It begins at Jerusalem, where they were, and follows them where they were scattered.

precepts.text: Beginning at Moses and all the prophets, he expounded unto them in all the scriptures the things concerning himself.
precepts.point: They could not match the prophecies to the life being lived in front of them. He had to open the scriptures himself, from Moses through all the prophets, to shew what they said of him.

note.label: John 5: The Pool of Bethesda and the Witness to the Son

precepts.why:
“Search the scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me.” The scriptures testify of Christ, but they could not match the prophecies to the life being lived in front of them.

He had to open the scriptures himself: “And beginning at Moses and all the prophets, he expounded unto them in all the scriptures the things concerning himself.” From Moses through all the prophets, he shewed what they said of him. The scriptures they searched were the ones testifying of him all along, and “ye will not come to me, that ye might have life.”

precepts.text: Thus it behoved Christ to suffer and rise the third day, and that repentance and remission of sins should be preached among all nations, beginning at Jerusalem.
precepts.point: "All nations" does not mean the Chinese or the Japanese. Prophetically it means the Israelites scattered among all nations: into Assyria (which is why Jonah preached to Nineveh, where the northern kingdom was exiled), then Babylon, Persia, Media, Greece, and Rome, then into Africa and out through the transatlantic and Indian Ocean slave trades. That prophecy did not happen only once; it happened all through history.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

precepts.why:
Luke gave a full historical account of everything Christ did, from his birth “Until the day in which he was taken up”, and the end of Luke segues straight into Acts. The commandments Christ gave through the Holy Ghost are right there: “Thus it is written, and thus it behoved Christ to suffer, and to rise from the dead the third day: And that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name among all nations, beginning at Jerusalem.”

“All nations” does not mean the Chinese or the Japanese. Prophetically it means the Israelites scattered among all nations: into Assyria, which is why Jonah preached to Nineveh, where the northern kingdom was exiled; then Babylon, Persia, Media, Greece and Rome; then into Africa and out through the transatlantic and Indian Ocean slave trades. That prophecy did not happen only once; it happened all through history. Repentance was to be preached to Israel wherever they were scattered.

precepts.text: Christ expounded all things written in the law of Moses, the prophets, and the psalms concerning him, then opened their understanding to understand the scriptures.
precepts.point: The gift of the Holy Ghost that follows is understanding being opened. Baptism with the Holy Ghost is the spirit of wisdom and understanding, seen when Christ opened the disciples' understanding to grasp the scriptures concerning him.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
Here is what the gift of the Holy Ghost looks like. Christ told the disciples “that all things must be fulfilled, which were written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning me. Then opened he their understanding, that they might understand the scriptures”.

He expounded everything written about him in the law of Moses, the prophets and the psalms, and then opened their understanding to grasp it. That opening of the understanding is the baptism with the Holy Ghost, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the gift Peter promises to those who repent and are baptized in the name of Jesus Christ.

precepts.text: The chief priests and rulers delivered him to be condemned to death and crucified him; those rulers are the "own" that received him not.
precepts.point: This five thousand disproves the Christian claim that the Jews all rejected Christ. He came unto his own, meaning the religious leaders, the builders, the chief priests and rulers whose job was to guide the nation, and only those upper echelons rejected him, while thousands of the people believed and were zealous of the law.

note.label: Acts 4: The Stone the Builders Rejected

precepts.why:
“And how the chief priests and our rulers delivered him to be condemned to death, and have crucified him.”

The chief priests and the rulers delivered him up. Those rulers are the own that received him not, not the five thousand men who heard the word and believed.

precepts.text: He opened their understanding that they might understand the scriptures; when you keep the laws, your understanding is opened, which is a form of receiving the Holy Ghost.
precepts.point: When the apostles at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of the Most High, they sent Peter and John, who prayed for them that they might receive the Holy Ghost. Notice the order: Philip, the deacon, woke up the city and planted, but the apostles had to come and put the spirit on them. It is the same order today, where the bishop and the apostles visit the cities where new schools open and pray over the congregation.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

precepts.why:
“Then opened he their understanding, that they might understand the scriptures”. When you keep the laws, your understanding is opened, and that is a form of receiving the Holy Ghost.

That is what the apostles came down to Samaria praying for. Philip planted, and the apostles put the spirit on them, opening their understanding of the scriptures.
